question: What security concerns exist in Flask's session handling?
gold_answer: Security concerns: (1) No secret_key = NullSession, writes silently fail. (2) Sessions signed with HMAC-SHA1 by default (digest_method = sha1). (3) BadSignature on tampered cookies returns empty session, doesn't reject request. (4) Cookie flags default to httponly=False, secure=False — XSS/CSRF risk. (5) Nested dict mutations not tracked — changes silently lost unless session.modified=True set manually. (6) Vary: Cookie only set if session accessed.
